headline: Impeachment Court Sets Two-Strike Rule for Sub Judice Violations
seoTitle: Impeachment Court Sets Two-Strike Sub Judice Rule | FMB News
seoDescription: The Senate Impeachment Court adopted graduated penalties for lawyers who publicly discuss the merits of Vice President Sara Duterte's trial.
deck: A first violation brings a public reprimand; later violations may draw a ₱30,000 fine and restrictions on a lawyer's participation in proceedings.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate Impeachment Court adopted a two-strike system for violations of the sub judice rule during Vice President Sara Duterte's trial, presiding officer Francis Escudero announced on August 26.

For lawyers representing the prosecution or defense, a first offense brings a public reprimand and admonition entered in the court record. A second and succeeding violation may result in the maximum statutory fine of ₱30,000 for each offense and restrictions on speaking, objecting or examining witnesses on the floor.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Escudero said earlier conduct would not be punished under the new ruling and that the standard would apply prospectively to all parties. He also encouraged both sides to designate spokespersons who are not among the lawyers appearing before the court.

Possible violations by senator-judges may be referred through a Senate ethics complaint. For lawyers, the court may transmit a certified incident record to the Office of the Bar Confidant, the Integrated Bar of the Philippines or the Supreme Court for possible disciplinary action.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The rule seeks to keep arguments over evidence and witness credibility inside the impeachment proceedings while giving participants advance notice of graduated sanctions. It does not decide the merits of the charges against Duterte.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch how the court applies the rule to future public statements and whether either side changes its media practice or appoints a non-counsel spokesperson.
